description.en:
Named individuals for the ISO/IEC 7498-1 ontology design pattern: the seven layers of the reference model, the protocol data units practice names per layer, common technologies of industrial communication, and the quality of service parameters.

They are kept apart from the pattern so that the terminology and the vocabulary can be maintained separately. A model importing only the pattern gets the classes; one importing this file gets the vocabulary as well, and need not declare that MQTT is an application layer technology for itself.

comments.en:
Three groups of individual, with different standing.

The seven layers are normative: ISO/IEC 7498-1, 6.1.2 enumerates them and gives each a number.

The protocol data units and the technologies are conventional. Frame, packet, and segment do not occur in the standard, and 1.3 states that it implies no particular technology. They are supplied because an engineering model needs them and because naming them once keeps models comparable. The list of technologies is open by design.

The quality of service parameters follow 7.4.4 for the four the standard names, and extend beyond it where practice requires, which is marked at the affected individuals.

note.value: ISO/IEC 7498-1, 5.2.1.11. Entities in the same layer are termed peer entities, 5.2.1.3, which this pattern expresses through the peerEntity relation rather than a separate class.

comment.en: An active element within a subsystem embodying a set of capabilities defined for the layer.

note.value: Reified so that a value can be annotated and referred to, in the same way and for the same reason as the flow of the VDI 3682 pattern. The parameter it belongs to is a named individual, the value and unit are literals of this model.

comment.en: The value a quality of service statement assigns to one parameter, together with its unit.

note.value: ISO/IEC 7498-1, 5.3 and 6.4. A connection is established before data transfer and released afterwards, so the transfer can rely on state held for its duration.

comment.en: A communication established, held, and released as a connection between the participating entities.

note.value:
**Collecting class of this pattern.** ISO/IEC 7498-1, 5.6.1 defines the three kinds below individually without naming a common superclass, and clause 5.6 groups them under the heading data-units.

Terms such as frame, packet, or segment do not occur in the standard: they are the names practice gives to the protocol data unit of a particular layer. The standard mentions framing only in a note to 7.6.4.5, which observes that the delimiting functions are sometimes referred to that way. Those names are supplied as individuals in ISO7498-instances.ttl, each related to its layer.

comment.en: A unit of information transferred between entities.

note.value: ISO/IEC 7498-1, 5.2.1.1. There is one and only one subsystem in an open system for a given layer, 5.2.2.1.

comment.en: An element in the hierarchical division of an open system which interacts directly only with elements in the next higher division or the next lower division of that open system.

note.value: ISO/IEC 7498-1, 5.2.1.9. One or more protocols may be defined for a layer, and an entity may employ one or more of them, 5.8.2.2. A protocol is the abstract set of rules; a technology is a concrete realisation named in practice.

comment.en: A set of rules and formats, semantic and syntactic, determining the communication behaviour of entities in the performance of their functions.

note.value:
ISO/IEC 7498-1, 5.1.3 c) names the associations as one of the four basic elements of OSI, joining the application entities and permitting them to exchange information.

The class name follows the standard and the readable label is communication, which is the plainer term for the same thing. The two are one class, not two: labelling rather than a second class avoids the drift that an equivalence between a standard term and an own term would invite.

comment.en: A relation joining open systems that permits them to exchange information.
A capability of a layer and the layers beneath it, provided to the entities of the next higher layer at the boundary between the two layers.

note.value:
ISO/IEC 7498-1, 5.2.1.2. Clause 6.1.2 enumerates exactly seven layers and numbers them from the physical layer as one to the application layer as seven.

The seven layers are named individuals rather than subclasses of this class. They are a closed enumeration of particular things, not kinds of thing, and as individuals they can carry their number as a value, which makes an ordering between them expressible. They are supplied in ISO7498-instances.ttl.
ISO/IEC 7498-1, 7.1.2. Consists of the application entities that cooperate in the OSI environment, 6.1.4.

comment.en: The highest layer, providing the sole means for an application process to access the OSI environment. It has no boundary with a higher layer.

note.value: ISO/IEC 7498-1, 7.4.2. Clause 7.4.4 names the quality of service parameters of this layer.

comment.en: Provides transparent transfer of data between session entities, relieving them of any concern with how reliable and cost effective transfer is achieved.
Provides the means to establish, maintain and terminate network connections between open systems and the means to exchange data units over them, independently of routing and relay considerations.
Provides for the representation of information that application entities either communicate or refer to in their communication, so that the syntax used is preserved in meaning.
Provides the mechanical, electrical, functional and procedural means to activate, maintain and de-activate physical connections for bit transmission between data link entities.
Provides the means for cooperating presentation entities to organise and synchronise their dialogue and to manage their data exchange.
Provides the functional and procedural means for the transfer of data between network entities and detects and possibly corrects errors occurring in the physical layer.
A subdivision of the OSI architecture, constituted by subsystems of the same rank.
The data transferred between entities on behalf of the entities of the next higher layer for whom they are providing services.

note.value: ISO/IEC 7498-1, 7.4.4 names throughput, transit delay, residual error rate, and establishment delay among the parameters of the transport service. Named individuals for these are supplied in ISO7498-instances.ttl, where the list stays open, since a model may need parameters the standard does not enumerate.

comment.en: The rate at which data is transferred over a communication.

note.value: Not named in ISO/IEC 7498-1, 7.4.4. Added because it is what makes a communication suitable or unsuitable for a control task.

comment.en: The variation of transit delay between successive transfers.

note.value: ISO/IEC 7498-1, 7.4.4. This is the parameter an engineering model uses to record latency.

comment.en: The elapsed time between the request to transfer data and its delivery.

note.value: ISO/IEC 7498-1, 7.4.4. Applies to connection-mode communication only.

comment.en: The elapsed time between the request to establish a connection and its confirmation.

note.value: Not named in ISO/IEC 7498-1, 7.4.4. Added because engineering models record it.

comment.en: The share of time a communication is usable.

note.value: ISO/IEC 7498-1, 5.10 mentions priority among the characteristics selectable through quality of service.

comment.en: The precedence a communication takes over others competing for the same resources.
The ratio of data lost, duplicated, or delivered incorrectly to data transferred in total.
A named characteristic of a communication, such as throughput or transit delay, that a quality of service statement assigns a value to.
Information exchanged between entities to co-ordinate their joint operation.

note.value:
ISO/IEC 7498-1, 5.10 and 7.4.4. The standard treats quality of service as a set of parameters selected by the entities and observed during the communication.

This is where a model records what a communication delivers rather than how it is built, which makes the class the anchor for non-functional properties of the communication subdomain.

comment.en: The characteristics of a communication, expressed through a set of parameters, that the participating entities can select and observe.

note.value: ISO/IEC 7498-1, 5.2.1.8. A service access point is attached to only one entity of its layer and to only one entity of the layer above at a time, 5.5.5, and both are in the same system, 5.5.2.

comment.en: The point at which the services of a layer are provided by an entity of that layer to an entity of the next higher layer.

note.value:
Addition of this pattern, not a class of ISO/IEC 7498-1. Clause 1.3 states that the fact a system is open implies no particular systems implementation, technology or means of interconnection, so the standard names none.

An engineering model has to record which protocol is used, which is why the class exists. Named individuals such as Ethernet, TCP, or MQTT are supplied in ISO7498-instances.ttl, each related to the layer it realises. Whether a given technology fits the layer a model claims for it is not checked here. Nothing stops a model from placing MQTT at the network layer, and rejecting that needs a rule base rather than an axiom, which keeps the pattern descriptive.

comment.en: Internet protocol version 4.
Gigabit Ethernet over twisted pair, 1000 Mbit/s.
Transmission control protocol, connection oriented.
User datagram protocol, connectionless.
File transfer protocol.
Fast Ethernet over twisted pair, 100 Mbit/s.
Frame based data link technology after IEEE 802.3.

note.value: Its master and slave access makes a segment two-way alternate in the sense of 5.3.1.15: both sides send, but never at the same time.

comment.en: Fieldbus for automation with master and slave access, after IEC 61158 and IEC 61784.
Real-time capable fieldbus technology on Ethernet, after IEC 61158.
Point to point communication with sensors and actuators, after IEC 61131-9.
Dynamic host configuration protocol.
Request and response protocol widely used in industrial equipment.
Communication protocol for embedded automation on CAN, after EN 50325-4.
Publish and subscribe messaging protocol for constrained devices, after ISO/IEC 20922.
Industrial Ethernet standard for automation, after IEC 61158 and IEC 61784.
Platform independent service oriented architecture for industrial interoperability, after IEC 62541.
Wireless local area network after IEEE 802.11.
Hypertext transfer protocol.
Advanced message queuing protocol, after ISO/IEC 19464.
Internet protocol version 6.
Hypertext transfer protocol over a transport layer security connection.
A concrete protocol or transmission technique realising the services of a layer.

note.value: ISO/IEC 7498-1, 5.6.1.3. Figure 9 shows that a protocol data unit of one layer becomes a service data unit of the layer below, which is the encapsulation the mapsToServiceDataUnit relation expresses.
Not a term of ISO/IEC 7498-1 in this sense. The standard uses segmenting as the name of a function, 5.8.1.9, that maps one service data unit onto multiple protocol data units.

comment.en: The protocol data unit of the transport layer.

note.value: Not a term of ISO/IEC 7498-1. Named by the network layer protocol standards.

comment.en: The protocol data unit of the network layer.

note.value: Not a term of ISO/IEC 7498-1. Named by the protocol standards of connectionless-mode services.

comment.en: The protocol data unit of a connectionless-mode transport or network service.

note.value: Not a term of ISO/IEC 7498-1. A note to 7.6.4.5 observes that the delimiting and synchronisation functions of the data link layer are sometimes referred to as framing, but the standard defines no such data unit.

comment.en: The protocol data unit of the data link layer.
A unit of data specified in a protocol, consisting of protocol control information and possibly user data.

note.value: ISO/IEC 7498-1, 4.1.3. A real system complying with the requirements of the OSI standards in its communication with other real systems is a real open system, 4.1.2. A device is not an open system in itself, it is one under the view this clause describes: those aspects of it that are pertinent to interconnection.

comment.en: The representation of those aspects of a real system that are pertinent to open systems interconnection.

note.value: ISO/IEC 7498-1, 5.6.1.4. A bit is the service data unit of the physical layer, 7.6.4.5 and 7.7.3.2, which is the one practice term the standard does name.
The one practice term ISO/IEC 7498-1 names: 7.6.4.5 refers to physical service data units, that is bits, and 7.7.3.3.1 to the transparent transmission of bit streams.

comment.en: The service data unit of the physical layer.
An amount of information whose identity is preserved when transferred between peer entities and which is not interpreted by the supporting entities.

note.value:
ISO/IEC 7498-1, 5.3.1.14 to 5.3.1.16 define three kinds of data communication by direction: two-way simultaneous, two-way alternate, and one-way. The three are supplied as named individuals in ISO7498-instances.ttl.

The direction complements the source and target systems rather than repeating them. Which systems send and which receive follows from hasSourceSystem and hasTargetSystem; whether both directions are possible at once or only in turn does not, and that is what this class records. A Profibus segment carries data in both directions but one at a time, which makes it two-way alternate, while a full duplex Ethernet link is two-way simultaneous.

ISO/IEC 7498-1, 5.3.1.15. The transmission underlying it is half duplex, 5.3.1.11, where an entity of the layer above chooses the direction. A master and slave bus segment is of this kind: both sides send, but never at once.

comment.en: Data communication in both directions, one direction at a time.

note.value: ISO/IEC 7498-1, 5.3.1.14. The transmission underlying it is duplex, 5.3.1.10. A full duplex Ethernet link is of this kind.

comment.en: Data communication in both directions at the same time.

note.value: ISO/IEC 7498-1, 5.3.1.16. The transmission underlying it is simplex, 5.3.1.12. A sensor reporting to a collector without receiving anything back is of this kind.

comment.en: Data communication in one pre-assigned direction.
The direction in which data communication takes place over a communication.

note.value: ISO/IEC 7498-1, 5.8.4. All the information required to deliver a service data unit, that is the destination address, the quality of service required, and any options, is presented together with the data in a single access.

comment.en: A communication in which each transmission is independent of every other and carries all the information needed to deliver it.

note.value: Addition of this pattern, connecting the reference model of clause 6 to the data units of 5.6.

comment.en: Relates a communication to a data unit conveyed over it.

note.value: Addition of this pattern. It records at which level of the reference model a communication is described, which is the question an engineering model asks and the standard leaves to the specific service definitions.

comment.en: Relates a communication to the layer whose services it uses.

note.value: ISO/IEC 7498-1, 6.5.1.1. Target means the destination of the data, that is the receiving system. See the note on hasSourceSystem for how the two express direction.

comment.en: Relates a communication to an open system data flows to.

note.value:
ISO/IEC 7498-1, 5.1.3 c). The standard places no upper bound on the number of participants: 5.3.1.4 calls a connection with more than two endpoints a multi-endpoint connection, and 5.3.1.9 defines data transmission as conveying service data units from one entity to one or more entities. No cardinality is asserted here, so one communication can carry a whole bus segment with its participants.

Super property of hasSourceSystem and hasTargetSystem, so a model that knows the direction states it through those, and a model that does not may still record who takes part.

comment.en: Relates a communication to an open system taking part in it, without stating the direction of the data flow.
The numeric quantity of a quality of service value.

note.value:
ISO/IEC 7498-1, Figure 9 and its note 3: a protocol data unit of a layer may be mapped one to one into a service data unit of the layer below, though other relationships are possible.

This is the encapsulation that recurs down the layers, and it is what makes the practice terms frame, packet, and segment unnecessary as classes: each is the protocol data unit of a particular layer, and the relation states how one becomes the payload of the next.

comment.en: Relates a protocol data unit of one layer to the service data unit of the layer below that carries it.

note.value: ISO/IEC 7498-1, 5.2.2.1: an open system is logically composed of an ordered set of subsystems, one per layer.

comment.en: Relates an open system to one of its subsystems.

note.value: ISO/IEC 7498-1, 5.2.1.1 and 5.2.1.11. Subsystems of the same rank collectively form a layer, and an entity exists within a subsystem of that layer.

comment.en: Relates a subsystem, an entity, or a data unit to the layer it belongs to.

note.value: Functional: one value quantifies exactly one parameter.

comment.en: Relates a quality of service value to the parameter it quantifies.
Relates a communication to the quality of service observed on it.

note.value: ISO/IEC 7498-1, 5.5.5: a service access point is attached to only one entity of its layer and to only one entity of the layer above at a time. Both are in the same system, 5.5.2.

comment.en: Relates a service access point to an entity attached to it.

note.value: ISO/IEC 7498-1, 5.2.1.3 defines peer entities as entities within the same layer. Symmetric, since the relation holds equally in both directions. Not every pair of peer entities can communicate, 5.2.2.2, so the relation records those that do.

comment.en: Relates an entity to an entity of the same layer with which it communicates.

note.value: ISO/IEC 7498-1, 5.6.1.3: a protocol data unit consists of control information and possibly user data, so this relation is optional.

comment.en: Relates a protocol data unit to the user data it carries.

note.value: ISO/IEC 7498-1, 5.2.2.1: a subsystem consists of one or several entities.

comment.en: Relates a subsystem to an entity within it.

note.value:
ISO/IEC 7498-1, 6.5.1.1 calls an open system that is the ultimate source or destination of data an end system. Source here means the origin of the data, that is the sending system, which is the reading the standard uses throughout.

Direction follows from how the two properties are filled rather than from a separate statement. A system named as source alone sends, one named as target alone receives, and one named on both sides both sends and receives, which is what makes a communication bidirectional. A bus segment names its master as source and its slaves as targets.

comment.en: Relates a communication to an open system data flows from.

note.value: ISO/IEC 7498-1, 5.8.2.2: an entity may employ one or more protocols, and meaningful communication requires the agreed selection of one, 5.8.2.3.

comment.en: Relates an entity to a protocol it employs.

note.value: ISO/IEC 7498-1, 5.6.1.3 and Figure 8. Figure 9 notes that no positional relationship between control information and user data within a protocol data unit is implied.

comment.en: Relates a protocol data unit to the protocol control information it carries.

note.value: Addition of this pattern. Asserted once per technology in ISO7498-instances.ttl, so that a model need only name the technology. Functional: a technology realises the services of one layer, and a protocol spanning two would be modelled as two technologies.

comment.en: Relates a technology to the layer whose services it realises.

note.value: ISO/IEC 7498-1, 6.1.2. Carrying the number as a value is what lets a query order the layers and ask which lies above which, without asserting an ordering relation between all pairs.

comment.en: The number of a layer in the reference model, from one for the physical layer to seven for the application layer.

note.value: Addition of this pattern, for the reason given at Technology. A communication may use several technologies, one per layer.

comment.en: Relates a communication to a technology realising it.

note.value: ISO/IEC 7498-1, 5.2.1.4 defines a sublayer as a subdivision of a layer, and 6.2.1 m) provides for creating them where distinct communication services need it.

comment.en: Relates a layer to the layer it subdivides.

note.value: A literal rather than a reference to a unit ontology, so that the pattern stays free of further imports. A model needing formal units can align this property to one.

comment.en: The unit of a quality of service value, for example ms or Mbit/s.
Relates an entity to a service it provides to the layer above.

note.value: ISO/IEC 7498-1, 5.3.1.14 to 5.3.1.16. Functional: a communication has one direction at a time. What the direction adds over the source and target systems is whether both directions are possible at once or only in turn.

comment.en: Relates a communication to the direction in which data communication takes place over it.
Relates a quality of service statement to one of its parameter values.
